parts.title: Campus Conversation: The Library Study Room
script: Narrator
Listen to a conversation between a student and a librarian.
Man
Hi, excuse me. Can you help me? I want to reserve a study room for my group.
Woman
Sure. Are you a student here? I need to see your student card.
Man
Yes, here it is. We have a biology project, and we need a quiet room on Thursday afternoon.
Woman
Let me check. Hmm, Thursday afternoon is very busy. All the large rooms are taken from one to five.
Man
Oh no. There are five people in my group. Is there anything else?
Woman
Well, we have small rooms, but they are only for three people. But wait, how about Thursday morning? Room 204 is free from nine to twelve. It has a big table and a screen for your computer.
Man
Morning... Two of my friends have a class at ten. Hmm. Can we use the room on Friday instead?
Woman
Friday is easier. Room 204 is free all day on Friday. But remember, you can only reserve a room for two hours at a time.
Man
Two hours? I thought we could stay longer. Our project is big.
Woman
I understand. That is the library rule, because many students need the rooms. But if nobody reserves the room after you, you can ask at this desk and stay another hour.
Man
Oh, that's good to know. OK, then Friday from two to four, please.
Woman
Done. Room 204, Friday, two to four. Please come on time. If you are more than fifteen minutes late, we give the room to another group.
Man
Fifteen minutes. Got it. I'll tell my group to come early. Thank you so much!
Woman
You're welcome. Good luck with your project.

questions.q: Why does the man go to the library desk?
o: To reserve a room for a group project
To ask about a library job
To find his lost student card
questions.exp: He says: 'I want to reserve a study room for my group.' Gist questions ask about the main purpose.

questions.q: Why can't the man get a room on Thursday afternoon?
o: All the large rooms are already taken
questions.exp: The librarian says: 'All the large rooms are taken from one to five.'

questions.q: Why doesn't the man accept the Thursday morning time?
o: Two group members have a class at ten
questions.exp: He says: 'Two of my friends have a class at ten.'

questions.q: Listen again: "Two hours? I thought we could stay longer." Why does the man say this?
o: To express surprise that the time limit is short
To complain that the room is too expensive
To say his project is finished
questions.exp: 'I thought...' shows he expected something different. He is surprised the limit is only two hours.

questions.q: What is the man's attitude at the end of the conversation?
o: Worried that his group will not come
questions.exp: He says 'Got it... Thank you so much!' — he is satisfied with the solution.

questions.q: What will the man probably do next?
o: Tell his group to arrive early on Friday
Go to his class at ten
questions.exp: He says: 'I'll tell my group to come early,' because of the fifteen-minute rule.

parts.title: Academic Lecture: Why Do Leaves Change Color?
script: Narrator
Listen to part of a lecture in a biology class.
Professor
Good morning, everyone. Today we will talk about a simple question: why do leaves change color in the autumn?
Professor
First, let's remember why leaves are green. Leaves have a chemical called chlorophyll. Chlorophyll is green. It helps the tree use sunlight to make food. This process is called photosynthesis.
Professor
In spring and summer, the days are long and there is a lot of sunlight. So the tree makes a lot of chlorophyll, and the leaves look green.
Professor
But in autumn, the days get shorter and the weather gets colder. Now the tree stops making chlorophyll. The green color slowly disappears.
Professor

And here is the interesting part. The yellow and orange colors were in the leaf all summer. We just could not see them, because the green color was too strong. When the green goes away, we can finally see yellow and orange.
Professor

Red is different. Red colors are made new in the autumn. Some trees, like the red maple, make red color when the days are sunny and the nights are cool. So, a sunny, cool autumn usually gives us very bright red leaves.
Professor

Finally, the leaves fall. Why? Well, in winter there is not much sunlight and water is often frozen. Keeping leaves would cost the tree too much energy. So the tree drops its leaves and rests until spring.
Professor
OK, for next class, please go outside and collect three leaves of different colors. We will look at them together.

questions.q: What is the lecture mainly about?
o: Why leaves change color in autumn
Why some trees have no leaves
questions.exp: The professor says: 'Today we will talk about... why do leaves change color in the autumn?'

o: It helps the tree make food from sunlight
questions.exp: 'It helps the tree use sunlight to make food.'

questions.q: According to the professor, why can we see yellow and orange in autumn?
o: The tree makes new yellow color
The green color goes away, so we can see them
The leaves get older and dry
questions.exp: Yellow and orange were there all summer; 'When the green goes away, we can finally see yellow and orange.'

questions.q: Listen again: "And here is the interesting part." Why does the professor say this?
o: To tell students an important point is coming
To change to a new class topic
questions.exp: This phrase prepares listeners for a key/important idea.

questions.q: What kind of weather gives very bright red leaves?
questions.exp: 'Red color... when the days are sunny and the nights are cool.'

questions.q: What will the students probably do before the next class?
o: Read a chapter about maple trees
Collect three leaves of different colors
questions.exp: Homework: 'collect three leaves of different colors.'
